content.text:
I don't think the PR should say "4x faster." I couldn't reproduce that number, so I drafted the description around what I could measure.

## What I found

- **Allocations didn't change.** `strings.Split` already counts separators and makes the slice once at the right size. With `-benchmem`, both versions make **1 allocation per call with the same number of bytes**. The code comment says the rewrite avoids `strings.Split` allocations, but it doesn't.
- **The results are mixed.** I benchmarked the new `Fields` against `strings.Split(line, ",")`, 5 runs each, with Go 1.26 on an M5:

  | Input | new | strings.Split | change |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 4 fields (`a,b,c,d`) | ~20 ns | ~24 ns | ~15% faster |
  | 7-field CSV row | ~62 ns | ~50 ns | **~20% slower** |
  | 201 fields | ~925 ns | ~1690 ns | ~1.8x faster |

  The output matches `strings.Split` exactly, including for empty input, a lone comma, and empty or trailing fields.
- **Nobody can rerun `bench.txt`.** The repo has no `BenchmarkFields`, so the input it used is unknown. It's a single run (`-count=1`) without `-benchmem`. The iteration counts (exactly 4,000,000 and 16,000,000) don't look like what `go test` normally reports. The 4x could depend on one particular input, or the file may not be raw benchmark output.

## Draft PR description

> **parser: replace `strings.Split` with a manual loop in `Fields`**
>
> `Fields` now scans the line once by hand instead of calling `strings.Split(line, ",")`. The output is unchanged: same fields, including empty and trailing ones.
>
> **Performance:** both versions allocate once per call, so the gain is CPU time only, and it depends on line length (Go 1.26, Apple M5, 5 runs each):
>
> | Input | Before | After |
> |---|---|---|
> | 4 fields | ~24 ns/op | ~20 ns/op |
> | 7-field CSV row | ~50 ns/op | ~62 ns/op |
> | 201 fields | ~1690 ns/op | ~925 ns/op |
>
> Lines with many fields get faster (~1.8x). Short and typical rows are about the same or slightly slower.
>
> 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Before opening the PR

- If you got 4x on a specific input, commit that benchmark with `-benchmem` and `-count≥5` and compare with `benchstat`, then I'll update the table. If your real rows look like the 7-field one, the change may not be worth merging.
- Fix the comment at `parser/parser.go:5`, since there are no allocations being avoided.

I didn't change anything in the repo. The benchmark ran in a temporary directory, which I've deleted.
